about: Read state (SPEC 19.27): kind 30078, d = belfry:read, NIP-44 v2 to the author's own key; content JSON {v,s,m,c,t,d}. Every number = read up to and including that unix second. merge = highest per mark, unknown fields kept (remote first). floor = max(now - 90 days, s) for c / t / m, now - 90 days for d. readUpTo = max(own mark, floor). prune drops marks <= floor, then the oldest while weight (UTF-8 key bytes + 16 each) > 40000, raising s to the newest dropped. covers(remote, local) = false means publish merge(local, remote) pruned.

cases.name: two devices: every mark is the highest of the two
merge is the same either way round
out of order: an older event arriving after a newer one changes nothing
unknown fields are kept: the relay copy first, then the local one; v is always written as 1
parse: bad numbers, arrays, null and keys over 200 characters are dropped; floats are floored
parse: not JSON / not an object gives the empty state
parse: an array gives the empty state
serialize: unknown fields first (sorted), then v s m c t d, map keys sorted, no spaces
readUpTo: own mark, else the floor; s is no floor for direct messages
mark: never backwards; keys over 200 characters ignored
prune: marks at or under their floor go (s for channels and threads, 90 days for everything); m and s stay
prune: over 40000 weight (UTF-8 key bytes + 16 per mark), the oldest marks go and s rises to the newest dropped
covers: the relay already has it all (equal or higher) → nothing to publish
covers: a newer channel mark here → publish
covers: a mark here under the relay floor (s) → nothing to publish
covers: a direct message mark the relay lacks, older than s (s does not apply to d) → publish
covers: a later start s here → publish
covers: mentions seen later than the relay says → publish
